note: Read the whole transcript (00:00-1:05:42). The 05:45-07:40 'motivated' stretch is one knot: a didn't-know (D1), one voiced recast of his form (D3), the la- preposition (D5), and a fumbled 'I drove' (D6); D2, D4 and D10 are pieces of the same moments or engine noise. The engine writes ta-marbuta the same whether -a or -et is spoken, so idafa -t rows (D8) cannot be proven from script alone. D6 and D12 need the audio: D6 may be a dropped qaf (S4) rather than a wrong form; D12 turns on whether Amal's one-word 'تلات' was a prompt or a th->t pronunciation echo. Challenged A3 (a question, not a use) and A12 (Amal confirmed both forms work).

row.medi_said: I really need the word, I really need the word for motivated.
row.amal_said: بس a good word for motivation motivated is متشجع.
row.why: He asked outright for the word for 'motivated'; Amal supplied حافز/دافع (motivation) then متشجع (motivated) and typed it - a didn't-know, tier 0.

rulings.why: Transcript 05:45 is a plain 'I need the word for X' and Amal answers it at 06:00/06:27 - a didn't-know, not a slip. r2 filed the same moment inside D2 (سبب -> متشجع); this is the one row for it.

Two different pieces, neither a second error. r2's piece (سبب -> متشجع, tier 0 asked) is the same didn't-know as D1 - he offered سبب and rejected it himself in the same breath ('No, sabab is a reason, right?'). r1's piece (دفع -> دافع): the engine wrote دفع at 06:00 while Amal spoke over him ('We know, we know motivation حافز أو دافع') - her line is a supply answering his 05:45 request, not a recast of a wrong form, and one clipped long vowel in a hesitant 'daafe3' is engine-level. Duplicate of D1 / cannot be verified.

row.why: First use of the word she had just given: the engine wrote شجّع with the shadda (shajja3, the doubled-middle 'make someone motivated' verb) where the state needs the participle متشجع; Amal recast متشجع at once (and again at 07:26 أنت ما كنت متشجع). Make-X vs get-X family (B12) and a participle (B15). Confusables note: if the audio shows shuja3 (brave) instead - he had linked the word to شجاع at 06:34 - the row becomes vocab-A tier 1 (brave for motivated); either way wrong -> right is the same.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; only the label differs. Ruled with the transcript's form (شجّع, shadda = the make-verb) -> grammar B12 (+B15 participle), with the shuja3 alternative noted for the merger.

Two pieces, both already covered. r2's piece (عشان -> لـ) is the same slip as D5 at 07:08 - kept there with the full row. r1's piece (شجاع let pass at 07:03) is his repeat of the line Amal had just recast at 06:57 ('مش، مش شجاع' nine seconds after her متشجع, she said مم) - GR-28: a repeat of the just-fixed line is one moment with D3, not a fresh vocab-B.

row.why: After مش متشجع he continued with عشان (because/for); Amal said لا, he took it as 'no' ('What do you mean لا؟'), and she named the rule 'It takes لا' and typed 'mitshajje3 + la' - the word picks its own preposition la-.

rulings.why: Clear in the transcript: his عشان at 07:08, her 'It takes لا' at 07:12 and the typed 'mitshajje3 + la' at 07:16. r2 folded the same slip into D4; one row, here.

row.chat: ana su2et la-saa3tain 3ala zabaayen kunet mit7ammesilhom u jebet aktar min 3eshreen sajjaade.
row.why: He said a form the engine wrote سويت four times while Amal could not place it (she guessed صرت, then gave the past of 'drive' - engine سألت, her chat 'ana su2et' shows the word was سقت); he said 'yeah' and repeated it (07:38) - a wrong form of ساق (sheet: 'i drove | su2et | سقت'), the -et ending was right so not B5. Audio must decide: if he said 'suwet' with a dropped ق it is S4 pronunciation and the row falls; if he said sawweet (I did) it is tier 1.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same moment; the transcript proves Amal voiced a fix he took ('yeah. أنا سألت' then ممتاز), but the engine's سويت cannot tell a wrong form from a dropped qaf. Kept low, vocab-A tier 2 (wrong form of a sheet word), flagged for audio.

Self-fix inside the same turn and no signal: 12:01 'لـ الإجتماع، للـ uh, yeah، إجتماع' ends on the bare إجتماع that matches her typed la-ijtimaa3, Amal said nothing about el- (she only answered his موعد/اجتماع question at 12:14), and جهزت للاجتماع is itself ordinary Arabic for a meeting the listener now knows about. Not an error (GR-22 / GR-19).

Cannot be an error from this transcript: Arabic script writes سيارة the same whether he said sayyaara or sayyaaret, so the engine cannot show a missing -t. Amal said ممتاز after سيارة (44:34) and again after أخوتي (44:40); her 'So for feminine nouns, what do we add?' is the rule check she runs after a right answer (he answered 'the T'), not a fix. Not supported.

row.medi_said: So after هذي and هدول and هناك and,
row.why: Listing the demonstratives he again named هناك (over there) as one of them; Amal prompted 'هناك is what?' and he fixed it himself ('not هناك. هذيك and هذاك'). Same wrong word as A14 (27:04) but 37 minutes later and prompted separately, so a second row, not a repeat of a just-fixed line.

rulings.why: Transcript 1:04:18-1:04:26 is exactly as r1 wrote it; a separate prompted fix long after A14, so it stands on its own.

His مش متشجع is present tense and right: it answers Amal's 05:36 كيفك ('I need the word for motivated' - his state now), and the story he then tells (yesterday I drove two hours ... they bought nothing) is the reason. Amal's 07:26 'أنت ما كنت متشجع' comes while he is fumbling سويت and reads as her tracking the story, not a recast; nothing in his next lines takes a ما كنت for this clause (his 08:17 كنت is the genuinely past 'I was excited'). Not an error; if audio shows he meant 'I wasn't motivated yesterday', it would be B6.

Not a negation slip of his: he had already said أنا كنت متحمس right at 08:26; the ما كنت at 08:49 echoes Amal's own question frame two seconds earlier ('ما كنت what؟ You weren't.'), and he corrected the meaning himself at once ('I was excited for-- How do I say customers I was excited for?') before she gave كنت متحمس إلهم. Parroting her prompt plus self-fix, no C4 rule applied wrongly.

Her one-word repeat reads as her usual prompt (like 'هناك is what?' / 'الـ'); if audio shows it was only a th->t pronunciation echo, the row becomes grammar-B E1 (let pass, then his own fix).

row.medi_said: ما، ما اشتروا. ما شطار. ما شطار.

row.why: He said ما اشتروا, then settled on a form the engine wrote ما شطار twice (no plural -u); Amal's prompt 'They are a group so they didn't' shows she heard a form that did not match the plural subject الزباين; he gave ما اشتروا, she said 'Yes'. His right form came before the wrong one, so not a self-fix. Engine may have mangled the second form.

rulings.why: Amal's prompt names the exact problem (plural subject, verb not plural), and he fixed it only after it - a voiced B18 correction. Medium, not low: her prompt is specific even if the engine's شطار is noisy.

challenges.why: 09:17 is a question, not a use: 'Who جيب، جويب. Is it-- It would be جابت؟ بجيب، جابت.' - he asked whether the past of بجيب is جابت and Amal answered جبت (then explained the vowel). The brief rules 'is it X or Y?' neither a slip nor a use; the next real use at 09:42/09:49 was جبت, correct. Keep for human check only if asking 'it would be جابت?' counts as an assertion.

24:05 هاديين -> هاديات: Amal offered the feminine as an option ('Or because they're women'), he asked 'هاديات?' (Yes), then said 'But they both work' and she agreed ('Mm-hmm'). Per the brief, when Amal says both forms are fine it is not a slip; the row rests on an optional recast she herself did not insist on.
